subject: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datadog.com>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@grafana.com>, Jules Martin <jules.martin@sentry.io>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)

Hi all,

We're kicking off a coordinated procurement request for observability add-ons (extended log retention, cold archival, and long-term event storage) across Datadog, Grafana Cloud, and Sentry. The goal: lock in predictable unit economics for 2027 while keeping the ability to shift between vendors by bundling credits at the organizational level.

We'd like each vendor to provide a simple committed-slab proposal with:
- 3 commit tiers (base/moderate/high) with monthly GB committed and corresponding per-GB effective price
- retention windows supported per tier (e.g., 30/90/365) and read/egress terms
- any add-on discounts for cross-product usage (metrics + logs + traces) and lookback access pricing
- minimum term and early-exit clauses (if any)

Please attach the pricing spreadsheet and a one-page term sheet. Internal recipients: Rishi, Monica, Marcus — please prioritize numbers and what acceptance criteria we should require from legal (SLA/evidence for egress limits/audit).

I attached an internal template for how we want the tiers filled out; feel free to return a populated spreadsheet or a short PDF term sheet.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Procurement (observability)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_obs_blended_commit_memo.pdf (internal template)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datadog.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a populated spreadsheet that maps to your three tiers and a short term-sheet. Summary upfront:

- Base: 50 TB/month commit — $0.023/GB effective (30-day retention)
- Moderate: 150 TB/month commit — $0.017/GB effective (90-day retention)
- High: 500 TB/month commit — $0.011/GB effective (365-day retention)

We can offer a further 7% blended credit if Redwood commits to a single annualized spend across Datadog logs + metrics (minimum $1.2M/yr). Egress for archived logs is billable at $0.03/GB unless you purchase the archival-read bundle (additional $0.002/GB on committed tier). Term: 12 months standard; early-exit is pro-rated shortfall with a 60-day cure period.

Attached: Datadog-commit-pricing-2026.xlsx and Datadog-term-sheet-12mo.pdf

From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@grafana.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datadog.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)

Thanks Vanessa — looping in our cloud retention team. Grafana can match a similar tiered structure with a slightly different shape:

- Tier A (50 TB/mo): $0.020/GB effective, 60-day retention by default with optional cold bucket for 365 days at +$0.003/GB
- Tier B (200 TB/mo): $0.015/GB effective, incl. 90-day hot retention + 275-day cold index
- Tier C (600 TB/mo): $0.010/GB effective, includes read credits for archival restores (2 restores / month included)

We can also offer a cross-product credit (Grafana + Loki + Mimir) if Redwood standardizes on Grafana for metric visualizations; that would be a 5% uplift on the effective discount. Term sheet attached: Grafana-Cloud-archival-term-sheet.pdf

On Thu, 9 Dec 2026 at 09:12, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> We're kicking off a coordinated procurement request...

—Ayesha
Grafana Cloud — Strategic Partnerships

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)

Vanessa / team — quick thoughts after reviewing vendor returns:

- Need normalized cost-per-GB that includes expected restore/egress behavior. The vendor "effective" rate often hides restore charges; ask for a 12-month modeled cost with 3 restore scenarios (0/2/10 restores per month).
- Sentry's storage addendum looks promising for error events but we must verify retention indexing cost vs. raw object storage.
- Can we require a 30-day SLA on archival restores for the higher tier, or at least a guaranteed RTO ladder?

Monica/Marcus: request approval to run a 1-page risk delta (price + SLA) to leadership for a blended commit. I'll throw together the 12-month model if you want.

—Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)

Marcus — forwarding vendor returns. Requesting exec approval to proceed with a blended commitment approach:

Proposal summary (one-line): commit to a blended annual spend across vendors with a tiered swap clause (quarterly re-allocation up to 25% between vendors) to get a 6–8% blended credit and reduce unit price on 90–365 day retention buckets.

Key asks from finance/legal before sign:
- Cap on archival egress (or fixed egress uplift)
- Clear RTO for restores at higher tiers and audit logging for restore events
- DocuSign-ready term sheet per vendor with early-exit and make-whole math

Attachments: redwood_obs_blended_commit_memo.pdf (internal summary), Sentry-storage-addendum.docx

Can you sign off or flag items to escalate? If approved, I'll route to procurement and legal and kick off DocuSign.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed committed-slab structure for observability add-ons (Datadog / Grafana / Sentry)

Monica / team — I reviewed the summary and the vendor spreadsheets. High level: I approve moving forward with the blended commitment pilot subject to three conditions:

1) Final legal term sheets include a hard cap on archival egress or a predictable uplift model (no open-ended egress buckets).
2) We get a 30-day RTO guarantee for Tier C restores or a clear SLA credit formula tied to restore latency.
3) Finance wants the final 12-month modeled cost (Rishi to provide the 0/2/10 restore scenarios) and the HubSpot record linked to the procurement package.

If those are satisfied, approve authority granted to Monica to execute up to $1.5M annual blended spend for the pilot. Route contracts to DocuSign once legal signs off.

Marcus Lin
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

References: HUBSPOT-REC-78321; DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/documents/OBS_COMMIT_5592
